theory.overview: Segment Tree is a binary tree data structure for range queries and point updates on arrays. Each node stores information about a segment (range) of the array. Supports range queries (sum, min, max, GCD) and point updates in $O(\log n)$ time. Build in $O(n)$. Used in competitive programming for range query problems. This chapter covers segment tree structure, operations, lazy propagation for range updates, and applications.

sections.title: Segment Tree Structure
sections.content: Binary tree where each node represents a segment of the array. Root represents entire array [0, n-1]. Left child represents [l, mid], right child represents [mid+1, r]. Leaf nodes represent single elements. Height = $O(\log n)$. Total nodes = $2n-1$ (or $4n$ for safe array allocation). Each node stores aggregate (sum, min, max) of its segment.

sections.title: Build Operation
sections.content: Build tree recursively from array. For leaf node, store array value. For internal node, combine children's values (sum = left + right, min = min(left, right), max = max(left, right)). Time: $O(n)$. Space: $O(n)$ for tree array.
sections.algorithm: build(node, l, r): if l == r: tree[node] = arr[l]; else: mid = (l+r)//2; build(left, l, mid); build(right, mid+1, r); tree[node] = combine(tree[left], tree[right]);

sections.title: Point Update
sections.description: Update single element at index. Recursively find leaf, update it, then recompute all ancestors. Time: $O(\log n)$. Propagate changes up the tree.
sections.algorithm: update(node, l, r, idx, val): if l == r: tree[node] = val; else: mid = (l+r)//2; if idx <= mid: update(left, l, mid, idx, val); else: update(right, mid+1, r, idx, val); tree[node] = combine(tree[left], tree[right]);

sections.title: Range Query
sections.description: Query aggregate over range [ql, qr]. Recursively traverse: if segment completely outside, return neutral. If completely inside, return node value. If partial, recurse on both children and combine. Time: $O(\log n)$.
sections.algorithm: query(node, l, r, ql, qr): if ql > r or qr < l: return neutral; if ql <= l and r <= qr: return tree[node]; mid = (l+r)//2; return combine(query(left, l, mid, ql, qr), query(right, mid+1, r, ql, qr));

sections.title: Lazy Propagation
sections.content: For range updates (add value to all elements in range). Lazy propagation defers updates until needed. Each node has lazy value (pending update). When visiting node, apply lazy to node, propagate to children. Enables range updates in $O(\log n)$. Complex but powerful.
sections.concept: Store pending updates, apply when needed

keyConcepts.name: Segment Representation
keyConcepts.description: Each node represents a contiguous segment of the array. Root = entire array, leaves = single elements.
keyConcepts.property: Segment [l, r] splits into [l, mid] and [mid+1, r]

keyConcepts.name: Combine Function
keyConcepts.description: Function to combine two child values into parent value. Depends on query type: sum = a+b, min = min(a,b), max = max(a,b), GCD = gcd(a,b).

keyConcepts.name: Neutral Element
keyConcepts.description: Identity for combine function. For sum: 0, min: ∞, max: -∞, GCD: 0. Used when segment is outside query range.

keyConcepts.name: Lazy Value
keyConcepts.description: Pending update to be applied to segment. Stored at node, propagated to children when needed. Enables efficient range updates.
keyConcepts.use: Range updates without updating all leaves immediately

steps.title: Build Tree
steps.description: Recursively build tree from array. Leaves store array values, internal nodes store aggregates.
steps.code: def build(node, l, r): if l == r: tree[node] = arr[l]; else: mid = (l+r)//2; build(left, l, mid); build(right, mid+1, r); tree[node] = combine(tree[left], tree[right]);

steps.title: Point Update
steps.description: Navigate to leaf, update value, recompute ancestors.
steps.code: def update(node, l, r, idx, val): if l == r: tree[node] = val; else: mid = (l+r)//2; if idx <= mid: update(left, l, mid, idx, val); else: update(right, mid+1, r, idx, val); tree[node] = combine(tree[left], tree[right]);

steps.title: Range Query
steps.description: Query range [ql, qr]. Combine results from relevant segments.
steps.code: def query(node, l, r, ql, qr): if ql > r or qr < l: return neutral; if ql <= l and r <= qr: return tree[node]; mid = (l+r)//2; return combine(query(left, l, mid, ql, qr), query(right, mid+1, r, ql, qr));

steps.title: Lazy Propagation - Apply
steps.description: When visiting node with lazy value, apply to node value and propagate to children.
steps.code: def apply_lazy(node, l, r, val): tree[node] += val * (r - l + 1); lazy[node] += val;

steps.title: Lazy Propagation - Push
steps.description: Before recursing, push lazy value to children.
steps.code: def push(node, l, r): if lazy[node] != 0: mid = (l+r)//2; apply_lazy(left, l, mid, lazy[node]); apply_lazy(right, mid+1, r, lazy[node]); lazy[node] = 0;

practiceProblems.title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
practiceProblems.description: Implement range sum with point updates using segment tree.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with sum as combine function. Build, update, query as described.

practiceProblems.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
practiceProblems.description: Multiple range sum queries on immutable array (prefix sum).
practiceProblems.solution: Prefix sum array. sumRange(i,j) = prefix[j+1] - prefix[i].

practiceProblems.title: Range Minimum Query
practiceProblems.description: Range minimum query with point updates.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with min as combine function. Neutral = ∞.

practiceProblems.title: Range Maximum Query
practiceProblems.description: Range maximum query with point updates.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with max as combine function. Neutral = -∞.

practiceProblems.title: Range Sum Query 2D
practiceProblems.description: 2D range sum with point updates.
practiceProblems.solution: 2D segment tree or 2D Fenwick tree. Segment tree of segment trees.

practiceProblems.title: Range Addition and Range Sum
practiceProblems.description: Range add (add value to range) and range sum queries.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with lazy propagation. Store sum and lazy at each node.

practiceProblems.title: Count of Range Sum
practiceProblems.description: Count range sums in [lower, upper].
practiceProblems.solution: Prefix sum + BIT/segment tree for counting prefix sums in range.

practiceProblems.title: Range Module
practiceProblems.description: Track ranges, add range, remove range, query if number in any range.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with interval tracking or ordered set of intervals.

practiceProblems.title: Falling Squares
practiceProblems.description: Simulate falling squares, track height after each drop.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with range max query and range update.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence
practiceProblems.description: Find number of LIS in array.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with (length, count) pairs. Coordinate compression.

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Pairs
practiceProblems.description: Count pairs i < j where nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree or BIT. Process from right, count smaller elements.
practiceProblems.hints: BIT or segment tree from right

practiceProblems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
practiceProblems.description: For each element, count smaller elements to its right.
practiceProblems.solution: BIT or segment tree. Process from right, query count of smaller.
practiceProblems.hints: BIT or segment tree from right

practiceProblems.title: Count of Range Maximum
practiceProblems.description: Count occurrences of maximum in range.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with (max, count) pairs.

practiceProblems.title: My Calendar I
practiceProblems.description: Book events if no overlap. Check if new event overlaps with existing.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree or ordered set of intervals.

practiceProblems.title: My Calendar II
practiceProblems.description: Book events if no triple overlap (max 2 events can overlap).
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree tracking overlap count. Or two ordered sets.

practiceProblems.title: My Calendar III
practiceProblems.description: Return maximum number of overlapping events after booking.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with range add and range max query.
practiceProblems.hints: Segment tree, range add, range max

practiceProblems.title: Range GCD Query
practiceProblems.description: Range GCD query with point updates.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with GCD as combine function.

practiceProblems.title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
practiceProblems.description: Range XOR query with point updates.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with XOR as combine function.

practiceProblems.title: Product of the Last K Numbers
practiceProblems.description: Product of last k numbers, handle zeros.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree or prefix product with zero tracking.

practiceProblems.title: Range Frequency Queries
practiceProblems.description: Count frequency of value in range.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree of hash maps or offline with Mo's algorithm.

practiceProblems.title: K-th Smallest in Range
practiceProblems.description: Find k-th smallest element in range.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree of sorted vectors with binary search.

practiceProblems.title: Majority Element in Range
practiceProblems.description: Find majority element (appears > n/2 times) in range.
practiceProblems.solution: Segment tree with (candidate, count) pairs using Boyer-Moore.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Subarrays with Bounded Maximum
practiceProblems.description: Count subarrays with max in [L, R].
practiceProblems.solution: Two pointers or segment tree with range max.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Well-Performing Interval
practiceProblems.description: Find longest interval where hours[i] > 8 for > half the time.
practiceProblems.solution: Transform to prefix sum, use hash map or segment tree.

practiceProblems.title: Create Sorted Array Through Instructions
practiceProblems.description: Cost to create sorted array (count smaller and larger elements).
practiceProblems.solution: BIT or segment tree for counting smaller/larger.
